sciXsRCLab: In a rock cycle diagram, what is the label for melted rock found underground?
Melted rock below Earth's surface is called magma.
Which type of rock forms when layers of sediment are pressed and glued together?
Sedimentary rock forms from sediment that is compacted and cemented.
Which type of rock forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting?
Metamorphic rock forms when heat and pressure change a rock while it stays solid.
In a rock cycle diagram, sand, mud and pebbles are all examples of…
Small loose pieces of rock such as sand, mud and pebbles are called sediment.
Granite forms from magma that cools slowly underground. Which label belongs on granite?
Granite forms from cooled magma, so it is an igneous rock.
Sandstone forms from grains of sand cemented together. Which label belongs on sandstone?
Sandstone is made of cemented sand grains, so it is sedimentary.
Marble forms when limestone is changed by heat and pressure. Which label belongs on marble?
Marble forms when limestone is changed by heat and pressure, so it is metamorphic.
Basalt forms when lava cools quickly at Earth's surface. Which label belongs on basalt?
Basalt forms from cooled lava, so it is an igneous rock.
Slate forms when shale is squeezed and heated deep underground. Which label belongs on slate?
Slate is shale changed by heat and pressure, so it is metamorphic.
Limestone often forms from layers of shells pressed together on the sea floor. Which label belongs on limestone?
Limestone forms from layers of shell pieces and other sediment, so it is sedimentary.
In a rock cycle diagram, which rock type is often shown with layers?
Sedimentary rock builds up in layers as sediment settles.
Which type of rock is most likely to contain fossils?

What label goes on the arrow where wind, water and ice carry sediment away?
Erosion is the moving of sediment by wind, water or ice.
What label goes on the arrow where rock is broken into smaller pieces by water, ice or plants?
Weathering is the breaking down of rock into smaller pieces.
What label goes on the arrow where sediment settles and piles up in layers?
Deposition is when moving sediment is dropped and settles in a new place.
Metamorphic rock that is heated until it melts becomes…
Any rock that melts underground becomes magma.
Igneous rock that is squeezed and heated deep underground, without melting, becomes…
Heat and pressure without melting turn rock into metamorphic rock.
Sedimentary rock that is broken down by weathering becomes…

No, rocks can follow many different paths
Yes, rocks always go igneous to sedimentary to metamorphic
Yes, rocks always start as metamorphic

Which energy source drives weathering and erosion at Earth's surface?

The pendulum speeds up as it falls to the lowest point.

Near the water, the diver is moving fastest and is lowest.

The stretched mat stores elastic potential energy, which then launches the jumper.

They lose energy and lock into place
They shrink

They lose energy and freeze in place

They speed up and spread even farther apart

Solid
Liquid

Gas particles move the fastest, so they have the most energy.
Why can you pour a liquid but not a solid block?
Liquid particles can slide past each other

Solid particles are far apart

Freezing
Melting

Melting
Evaporation
Sublimation

It rises quickly
It drops below 0 °C right away

All particles boil at once

Particles get bigger and float away

They are pushed closer together
They grow bigger
They become a solid immediately
They disappear

The temperature at which it changes from solid to liquid
The temperature at which a gas becomes a liquid
The temperature at which it boils
The coldest temperature possible

The metal's particles spread apart, so the lid expands
The glass shrinks to nothing
The lid's particles get bigger
Hot water makes the lid melt

sciXsDirF: A ball rolls to the left across a carpet. Which way does friction act on it?
Friction acts opposite to the direction of motion.
You push a shopping cart forward. Which way is your force?
A push acts in the direction you push.
A boy pulls a sled up a hill with a rope. Which way does the rope pull the sled?
Up the hill, along the rope
A pull acts along the rope toward the person pulling.
A skydiver falls toward Earth. Which way does air resistance push on the skydiver?
Air resistance acts opposite to the motion, so it pushes up on a falling skydiver.
A magnet pulls a paper clip toward it from the right. Which way does the magnetic force act on the paper clip?
To the right, toward the magnet
To the left, away from the magnet
An attracting magnet pulls the paper clip toward itself.
A boat floats on a lake. Which way does the water push on the boat?
The water's buoyant force pushes up on the boat.
A hockey player hits a puck toward the east. Which way does the stick push the puck?
The stick pushes the puck in the direction it sends it.
A car drives forward on a road. Which way does air resistance push on the car?
Air resistance acts against the direction of motion.
A person stands on the floor. Which way does the floor push on the person?
The floor pushes up with a normal force that balances gravity.
A person stands on the floor. Which way does gravity pull on the person?
Gravity always pulls objects down toward Earth's centre.
Two teams play tug-of-war. The team on the left pulls. Which way is their force on the rope?
The left team pulls the rope toward themselves, to the left.
A soccer ball rolls east across grass. Which way does friction act on the ball?
Friction acts opposite to the motion, so it points west.
A swimmer kicks the water backward. Which way does the water push the swimmer?
The water pushes back on the swimmer in the opposite direction, which is forward.
A bird flaps its wings downward. Which way does the air push the bird?
Pushing air down makes the air push the bird up.
A balloon is let go and air rushes out of its back end. Which way does the balloon move?
The escaping air pushes the balloon in the opposite direction.
A spring is stretched by pulling it to the right. Which way does the spring pull back on your hand?
A stretched spring pulls back toward its starting length, opposite your pull.
A box sits still on a flat floor. Which two forces act on it?
Gravity down and the normal force up
Gravity pulls down and the floor pushes up, so the box stays still.
A child on a swing is pushed forward from behind. Which way is the push?
The push acts in the direction the child is pushed.
A wagon is pulled to the right on a sidewalk. Which way does friction act on the wagon?
Friction opposes the motion of the wagon.
A ball is thrown straight up. While it rises, which way does gravity pull on it?
There is no gravity while it rises
Gravity pulls down on the ball the whole time, which is why it slows and falls back.
A paper airplane glides forward. Which way does air resistance (drag) push on it?
Drag acts opposite to the direction the airplane moves.
A tow truck pulls a car toward the north. Which way is the pulling force on the car?
The tow truck pulls the car in the direction it is moving the car.
